summary: A search of one folder is made by the names the index has the folder under, whatever path it was given by. In crates/fffinder-core/src/engine.rs, `Engine::root_spelling` asks the disk where the folder is (std::fs::canonicalize, before any lock is taken) for every search of one folder, and a new private pure function `index_spelling(scope, real, roots, follows_links)` says how to spell it: as given when a search location has it under exactly that spelling; the location's spelling plus the folder's real names when it is really inside a location (given with `..`, through a link, or in another letter case); its real path, searched through a temporary index, when it only looks as if it were inside one (a link or a `..` leads out); as given when it neither looks inside a location nor is in one. With Follow symbolic links on, a linked folder keeps the link's name, which that index has; a `..` or a path that differs from the disk's in letter case alone is still resolved. `search` and `grep_cancellable` respell their folder once and go on (they used to call themselves), and `prepare` waits for the index the search will use. Added in review: the engine keeps, in `Changes`, the name it searched each of the last 16 respelled folders by (`RESPELLED_KEPT`, `Changes::searched_as`), and `changes_for` goes by it, so the results of such a search follow the files that come and go in the folder like any other search's. The window, the server and the Nushell module are untouched. Files: engine.rs, docs/manual.md (one sentence in the scope bar's "Folder name" row), docs/protocol.md (the sentence on `scope`), tests/finder.rs, tests/controls.rs.
changelog: **Search Only in "Folder name"** found nothing in a folder that the window had reached by anything but its plain path: with `..` in the path, as after `fffinder ../lib` on macOS and Linux or Go to Folder with `..`; through a symbolic link inside a search location, while **Follow symbolic links** is off, as it is at first; or, on macOS and Windows, by a path typed in another letter case than the folder's, such as `~/documents`. The window showed the folder's items, and every search of it said No Results. Such a folder is now searched where it really is, and the results show that place. A linked folder that leads outside the search locations gets a temporary index, like any folder there. `--here`, `fff find` and `fff search` with `--scope` or `--here`, and `scope` in `/v1/find` and `/v1/search` follow the same rule.
behaviour_changes: All of these are for a search of one folder: Search Only in "Folder name", `--here`, the file chooser, a Smart Folder with a folder, `fff find` / `fff search` with `--scope` or `--here`, and `scope` in /v1/find and /v1/search. A search of This Computer is untouched.

A folder with `..` in its path (after `fffinder ../lib` or `fffinder ..` on macOS and Linux, Go to Folder with `..` on every system, a `scope` with `..`) is searched, by name and by contents. Before: No Results. Run: four tests, my own picture (review-dot-dot.png against the implementer's before-dot-dot.png), and the real app under Xvfb (first launch `fffinder ../beacon --query readme --here` from Projects/atlas listed beacon/README.md; a second launch `fffinder .. --query atlas --here` listed the 6 items under Projects).

A folder given or opened through a symbolic link inside a search location, with Follow symbolic links off (the default), is searched. Its results are listed where they really are: the Folder column shows the link's target, not the link. Before: No Results. Run: engine test, picture review-link.png, real app (hand-off of `Linked`).

A folder that a link or a `..` leads to outside every search location (`~/data -> /mnt/data`, `fffinder ../../Downloads --here` from inside a location) is searched through a temporary index of the real folder, like any folder outside the search locations: the first search says Indexing… until it is built, and results are spelled by the real path. A `..` that leads to the folder above a search location gets a temporary index of that folder, as its plain path already did. Before: No Results. Run: engine test, picture review-link-outside.png, real app (hand-off of `Away`).

macOS and Windows, by reading only: a folder typed in another letter case than the disk's (`fffinder ~/documents --here`, Go to Folder with a lowercase path) is searched by its real names. By the same path through canonicalize, so is one typed in another Unicode form than the name is stored in (macOS) and one given by an 8.3 short name (Windows).

With Follow symbolic links on: a linked folder is searched under the link's name as before (same results, same spelling); a `..` is now resolved, and so is a path that differs from the disk's in letter case alone.

/v1/find and /v1/search with such a `scope` return the folder's rows. Run against the real app: the plain path, the `..` spelling and the link gave the same 4 and 3 paths, and the link leading outside the same 3 as the folder's plain path. `fff find --here` / `fff search --here` in a folder the shell is in through a link: by reading (they send `$env.PWD`).

New in review: the results of a name search of such a folder follow the files that come and go in it. Before the review's fix the search listed the folder's files and then never showed a new one until something was typed, because the window asks the engine about its search with the folder as the window spells it, and the index reports files by its own names. Run in the real app with real watchers: a file made in the folder appeared in the list about 4 s later for the `..` spelling, for the link inside the search location and for the link leading outside it; a file with the word made outside the folder did not.

Cost: every search of one folder asks the disk once where the folder is (twice for a search with a sort other than relevance, which searches twice) and takes one short lock, on the search's background thread, never the window's. The implementer measured 2 to 3 microseconds for a local folder 7 to 9 names deep. Before, a folder that began with a search location as text was not looked up on disk. On a stalled network folder that call holds that folder's search back.

Unchanged: a folder spelled as the index has it (every plain spelling, a trailing slash, `./`, a doubled slash, a folder with a space and brackets, a missing folder, a file given as the folder), and a folder that is outside the search locations by its looks and in fact, which is still searched as given (so `outside/far/../far` still lists its results spelled with the `..`).
`Engine::prepare` waits for the index the search of that folder will use. No signature changed.
left_out: The folder is not cleaned where it comes in, so the window itself still holds it as given. Older than the branch and in the last release, and outside this brief's fault (finding nothing), but visible in the brief's own scenario; see Found, not fixed in notes. The brief's third test idea, a unit test of `start_location`, has nothing to test: `start_location` is untouched.

`Engine::folder_stats` / `folder_stats_for` still take the folder as the window spells it, so Calculate All Sizes and the git marks show nothing in a window whose folder is spelled another way (by reading). Not search, and as before.

With Follow symbolic links on: a path that goes through a link and also differs in letter case, or that differs from the disk's names in Unicode form (macOS) or by an 8.3 short name (Windows), is still searched as given and finds nothing, as before. With the setting off (the default) these are resolved, by reading.
Linux folders that ignore case (ext4 casefold, vfat): glibc's realpath keeps the case it is given, so nothing changes there.
A link whose target is a hidden folder inside a search location that is not a git repository still finds nothing with Follow symbolic links off: the index holds no hidden files.

No guard for a search location whose real path changed after its index started (a folder above it renamed in another letter case on macOS, a link above it pointed elsewhere). `RootIndex.canonical` is read once, so a plainly spelled folder there then looks as if a link led out of the location and gets a temporary index of its own: it is still found, more slowly, until fffinder starts again. Before, that case was searched in place.

No UI test for the link cases or for a folder outside the search locations: the temporary index scans on real threads and the harness clock is fake. They are covered by the engine tests and were run in the real app.
README.md is unchanged: it states nothing the change makes wrong. CHANGELOG.md is untouched, as the guide requires; the entry is in this record and in the commit message.

review_fixes: A search of a respelled folder listed files that the engine then said were none of its business. `Engine::changes_for` is asked by the window, on the window's thread, with the folder as the window spells it, and narrows the files the index reported by that spelling; the index reports them by its own names. So with the implementer's commit a search of `Projects/atlas/..`, of a linked folder or of one typed in another letter case found the folder's files and then never showed a new one, where a search of the plainly spelled folder shows it in a few seconds (live results are this branch's own feature). The implementer had listed it as left out. The engine now keeps the name it searched each of the last 16 such folders by, set by `root_spelling` at every search and dropped when a search finds the folder as given, and `changes_for` goes by that name; it asks no disk. The existing test of that contract, what_a_search_lists_is_among_the_changes_that_matter_to_it, has two such searches added and fails on the implementer's commit; a_search_is_told_which_changes_are_its_business tests the rule by itself; the new UI test a_search_of_a_folder_given_with_dot_dot_follows_that_folder fails without the fix; and the real app showed a new file by itself for all three kinds of folder.

docs/manual.md: one sentence in the scope bar's "Folder name" row. The results of a search of a folder opened through a link now show another place than the window's folder, which the manual said nothing of: "A folder you opened through a symbolic link is searched where the link points, and its results show that place, unless Follow symbolic links is on".

The local `respelled` at the top of `search`, `grep_cancellable` and `prepare` is named `as_indexed`. The pending accented-names-search change has a `respelled` of its own further down in `Engine::search` (the search's words in another spelling), and the two would have shadowed each other once both were on the trunk.
Commit message: a paragraph on the review's fix and a line on the two documentation edits. The Changelog paragraph is the implementer's, which I checked against the code and found true.

Nothing else was changed. `index_spelling`, its unit test and the three engine tests are the implementer's line for line.

For each, root_spelling gave the spelling I had written down beforehand, gave none when asked again with its own answer, and a name search and a contents search of the folder found exactly the files a walk of the real folder finds, each once. All 26 plain rows came back as given. (4) check.sh printed CHECK OK three times: on my fixes over ddefe96 (818 passed), after the rebase onto ffb02de (822), and on the trunk commit over 5e68c44 (829 passed in 16 test binaries, 3 of 3 known root-only failures). (5) The real app under Xvfb with its own settings and data folders and a copy of the demo folder as the only search location: the launches, the three new files and the /v1/find and /v1/search requests listed under behaviour_changes. The copy, with its two links, was in my scratch folder and is deleted.

Where the change is. The orchestrator's note asks for the change where the folder comes in unless the engine's root_spelling is clearly the smaller and safer place. The implementer chose the engine and I agree after reading both sides: the folder comes in at five places (start_location, the hand-off in run(), Finder::open_request, the server's `scope`, Go to Folder), and two ways in pass none of them: a linked folder opened by a double-click inside the window, and `fff find --here`, which sends $env.PWD. The entry could not give the letter case on Windows without `\\?\` paths either. Cleaning the entry as well would be an addition for the window's own state (see Found, not fixed), not a replacement.

The three ways I thought this most likely to hurt a user, and what the code and the runs say. (1) A plainly spelled folder that was searched in place is found no more, or only through a temporary index, because the disk's answer and the index's names differ. index_spelling changes nothing when a search location's spelling of the real path equals the folder as given, compared name by name, so it comes down to canonicalize returning each name as the index's walker read it. On Linux realpath never changes a name, and all 26 plain rows of my probe and every folder search in the 829 tests is as before. On macOS and Windows it is by reading, and by what I know of the two systems without having run them: macOS's realpath takes each name from the file system (getattrlist), Windows's from GetFinalPathNameByHandle, and the `\\?\` form only ever meets the search location's own canonical path, which has it too. Any failure of canonicalize leaves the folder as given. Two edges remain, both in left_out or below: a search location whose real path changed after its index started, and a disk on which realpath reports another spelling than a listing does. (2) Results from another place than the folder shown, from outside it, or a list that goes stale. The disk resolves `..` and links for canonicalize as it does for the window's own listing, so it is the same folder; the prefix check in search_root and grep_cancellable is made with the respelled folder; my probe compared every search with a walk of the real folder; the UI tests hold that Budget.csv outside Projects isn't listed. The stale list was real and is fixed (review_fixes). (3) A search that suddenly costs much more: a link or a `..` that leads outside the search locations now builds a temporary index of the folder it leads to, which can be a whole volume (`~/nas -> /Volumes/NAS`, or a `..` above the search location). That is what Search Only in already did for the same folder opened by its plain path, the window says Indexing…, three such indexes are kept at most, and with Follow symbolic links on the folder is searched in the location's own index as before. The extra disk call per search is a few microseconds on a local disk and runs on the search's thread.

Doubts for the owner. 1. macOS and Windows were not run; that half is by reading, and the fix leans on canonicalize as described above. To try on a Mac: (a) `cargo test -p fffinder-core a_folder_given`, where the letter-case test really runs and the link test goes through /var -> /private/var; (b) with home as a search location, `fffinder ~/documents --query <a word in a name there> --here`: the folder's matches, where it said No Results; (c) Search Only in a folder with an accented name, opened the normal way: still finds its items; (d) Go to Folder with `../<a sibling>`, then Search Only in; (e) a folder under /tmp given as `/private/tmp/...`; (f) a linked folder, with Follow symbolic links off and on; (g) with a search showing in a folder opened through a link or with `..`, make a file there whose name has the word: it should appear by itself within a few seconds. 2. A disk on which realpath reports another spelling of a name than a listing does would lose a search that works today. I know of none in ordinary use, but I could not rule it out for macOS volumes that are not APFS or HFS+ (exFAT, FAT, SMB): there realpath may return the name a folder was first looked up by, in whatever letter case that was, and a plainly opened folder would then be searched by that spelling and find nothing. If a search location on such a volume ever says No Results for a folder that plainly has matches, this is where to look. The sure cure would be to ask the index whether it has the folder as given before respelling it (fff-search's find_dir_index is private; `get_dirs()` can be walked), which I judged too large a change for a review. 3. The letter-case engine test has never run its body: on Linux `docs` is not `Docs`. On macOS and Windows CI it is its first real run. If it fails there, the letter-case half does not work on that system and nothing else is affected; the rule itself is pinned by the unit test. 4. The kept names are 16 at most. A seventeenth folder searched by another name than it was given by, while sixteen such searches are on screen, makes the oldest one stop showing new files until it is searched again.

For briefs still to come. - fix-folder-search-own-name-pool: `search_root` and the grep loop always get the folder spelled as the index has it, so `scope.strip_prefix(&base)` holds for folders given with `..`, through a link or in another case too. `search` and `grep_cancellable` begin by shadowing `req` with that request (`as_indexed`); use `req.scope` only below those lines. root_spelling no longer returns early for a folder that begins with a search location. - accented-names-search (lane b, in review): your commit merges with this one without conflict as it stood at 5778943. In `Engine::search` my local is `as_indexed`, so your `spelled` and `respelled` clash with nothing. In `changes_for` I shadow `req` just above the `let scope = req` statement and left that statement and `may_list` as they were, so your change to `may_list` applies as it is. `index_spelling` compares names in lowercase to tell a path that differs in letter case alone when Follow symbolic links is on; your `as_compared` could take the place of `to_lowercase` there to cover a name stored in another Unicode form, if you want it. - near-miss-beside-scattered (lane d, in review): no overlap; it merges cleanly as it stood at 46e0801. - adhoc-index-feedback: a temporary index is now also built for a folder that a link or a `..` leads to outside the search locations, and it is kept under the folder's real path, not the path the window has. Anything that looks for the window's folder in `indexes.adhoc` by path (progress for the folder shown, reuse for subfolders) has to respell it first: `Engine::prepare` does, through root_spelling, which asks the disk and so isn't for the window's thread. On the window's thread, `ChangeLog.respelled` has the name the last search of the folder used. - go-to-folder-keyboard: tests/controls.rs search_only_in_finds_the_items_of_a_folder_gone_to_with_dot_dot types `..` in Go to Folder, presses Return and asserts that the window's folder is `Projects/atlas/..` as typed. If Return starts taking a suggestion, or the dialog starts cleaning the path, that one assertion has to change; the search assertions after it hold either way. - regex-content-search: `grep_cancellable` begins with the `as_indexed` lines; put the regex branch below them, where `req.scope` is the folder as the index has it. - query-history-boost: nothing changes for track_open; the results of a respelled folder search have paths as the index spells them, so `path.starts_with(&r.path)` holds for them.

Found, not fixed (all older than this change). - The window's own state for a folder with `..` at the end of its path, as `fffinder ..` and Go to Folder with `..` leave it: `display_name` gives the whole path for it, so the title, the scope chip and the No Results text read "/home/.../atlas/.." (in after-dotdot.png the chip is so long that Any Kind wraps to a second line), and Enclosing Folder (`go_up` uses `folder.parent()`) goes to the folder below instead of the one above. `fffinder ../lib` is named "lib" and looks right, but Enclosing Folder leads to `.../app/..` from it. This is in the last release too and is worth a brief of its own: take the folder's real path where it comes in when the path has a `..` in it (start_location and the hand-off in run() in src/lib.rs, Finder::open_request, and `listing::resolve_typed_path` for Go to Folder, which joins what is typed on every system); std::path::absolute already does it for PATH on Windows. - `Engine::folder_stats` and `folder_stats_for` take the folder as the window spells it: no folder sizes and no git marks in a window whose folder is spelled another way than the index has it (by reading). - By reading: `set_search_settings` empties the indexes and sets the search locations again in two steps, and a search of a folder in between sees no locations and builds a temporary index for a folder that is inside one. - By reading: on Windows, where fff-search spells a search location in full and the settings may have a short name in it (`C:\Users\RUNNER~1`), `changes_for` never narrows the reported files by a search's folder, because the folder doesn't begin the way the index's paths do. Searches of one folder there run again for a matching file anywhere; the answer isn't shown unless the file is in it, so nothing wrong appears. - Met while running the real app with its data folder deep in the scratchpad: when the path of the data folder is so long that `run/fffinder.sock` passes the system's limit for a socket's path (104 bytes on macOS, 108 on Linux), the server doesn't start, fffinder says nothing of it (a log::warn that nothing shows), and it runs without one: a second launch opens a second app, and the Nushell commands find nothing to talk to. On macOS that takes an account name of more than about 40 characters. FFFINDER_SERVER_TCP=1 goes around it.
